reuse.why: Extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend with holidays and reuses recurConfigToRSchedule/RSchedule, but app.ts inlines `d.isWeekend(date) || isHoliday(...)` instead of reusing isSkippedDay, and the new range handler re-does the per-occurrence adjustment rather than sharing getUpcomingDates' mapping.

duplication.why: The 'daily: skip, otherwise move' decision is written three times (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange), and the weekend-or-holiday test is repeated inline twice next to the private isSkippedDay.

placement.why: Holiday matching and the move loop sit correctly in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip rule, which is schedule date policy, is decided at each caller in server/schedules/app.ts rather than in the shared module.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the date rules, the new handler, the RecurConfig field and tests.

maintainability.why: A future change to the daily or holiday rule must be made in three call sites, and schedule-template.ts still calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend without holidays or the daily rule, so paths already disagree.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange re-implement isSkippedDay inline and decide the daily rule themselves instead of a shared adjust-occurrence function; server/budget/schedule-template.ts left on the old getDateWithSkippedWeekend call

disguised_duplication.where: the daily-skip/move mapping appears as a nested ternary in getUpcomingDates, an if-chain in getDatesInRange and an occurrence loop in getNextDate; isSkippedDay's body is inlined as `d.isWeekend(date) || isHoliday(...)` in app.ts

abstraction_drift.where: shared/schedules.ts getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; the daily special case lives outside it at getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange; getUpcomingDates/getDatesInRange inline isSkippedDay and schedule-template.ts bypasses the new rules
